ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic disease to thyroid from other primary site

s1.syndrome_frame: Neck mass with dysphagia and pain, with a history of previous malignancy
salient_findings: Large, firm, mildly tender mass on the right side of the neck
Positive Pemberton sign
Hypo- to anechoic mass replacing the right thyroid lobe on ultrasound
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy suspicious for primary or secondary malignancy
Pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases on CT
key_facts: History of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans excision in 1998
Right lobe volume of 50 mL on ultrasound
Left lobe volume of 7.3 mL on ultrasound
Hemorrhagic background with isolated clusters of pleomorphic round and oval nuclei on fine-needle aspiration biopsy
Freely mobile vocal cords on laryngoscopy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans excision in 1998 with four local recurrences and external radiotherapy, combined with the presence of a large, firm, and mildly tender mass on the right side of the neck and a hemorrhagic background with isolated clusters of pleomorphic round and oval nuclei on fine-needle aspiration biopsy, suggests metastasis to the thyroid from the patient's known primary site.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The fine-needle aspiration biopsy results do not specifically suggest papillary thyroid carcinoma, and the patient's history of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a more likely explanation for the thyroid mass.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not provide evidence of follicular thyroid carcinoma, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with a metastatic lesion.

rejected.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results do not indicate anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, and the patient's age and clinical presentation are not typical for this aggressive tumor type.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease to thyroid from other primary site
rejected.why: While metastatic disease to the thyroid is possible, the patient's known history of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans makes it more likely that the thyroid mass is a metastasis from this primary site rather than another unknown site.
